definitions.explanation: The way a character or word is read or pronounced.
The ability to read or understand; one's interpretation of a situation.

examples.japanese: この{漢字|かんじ}の{読|よ}みがわからない。
examples.english: I don't know how to read this kanji.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{状況|じょうきょう}の{読|よ}みが{深|ふか}い。
examples.english: He has a deep understanding of the situation.

examples.japanese: {音読|おんよ}みと{訓読|くんよ}みを{覚|おぼ}えよう。
examples.english: Let's learn the on'yomi and kun'yomi readings.

notes:
{読|よ}み is the noun form of {読|よ}む (to read). It can refer to pronunciation or to one's interpretation/analysis of a situation.

KANJI READING TYPES:
- {音読|おんよ}み: Chinese-derived reading (on'yomi)
- {訓読|くんよ}み: Japanese-native reading (kun'yomi)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- {読|よ}みが{浅|あさ}い: shallow reading/analysis
- {読|よ}みが{深|ふか}い: deep reading/insight
- {読|よ}みが{甘|あま}い: naive interpretation
- {読|よ}みを{誤|あやま}る: to misread (a situation)

In games like shogi or go, {読|よ}み refers to reading ahead—predicting future moves.
